text:
Nick Suzuki is Montreal's captain and the reigning Selke Trophy winner, and 17 points in 15 games is what a first-line center is supposed to look like. He missed a stretch between Oct. 20 and Nov. 5, and he still averages 20.9 minutes a night.

Some of the pace is borrowed. He has 8 goals on 5.6 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 21% against a usual range of about 13 to 18. The bigger cushion: the Canadiens have scored 5.9 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which is why our numbers have him due to cool. His last ten games, 10 points against the 11.3 we'd expect, already read more ordinary.

The engine underneath is real. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 3.8 wins last season, 4th among 401 forwards, against competition in the 99th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man (9.1 primary shot assists per 60). Watch the power play, which has 7 of his points: Sportsnet's Eric Engels posted that Suzuki said "it's definitely not broken" on the day of the Rangers loss, and that by that night it was "shattered."
